official.label: Wizards of the Coast prerelease archetype guide

draft.label: Premier Draft
draft.headline: Learn what each colour pair is trying to do.
draft.guidance: These are the official Draft themes. Check that the enablers and payoffs reach you before committing; the order below is not a power ranking.

sealed.label: Sealed
sealed.headline: Find the strongest deck in your six packs.
sealed.guidance: Compare colour depth, early creatures, removal and castable threats. Use these ten plans to check your pool’s support; a signpost alone is not a reason to choose its colours.

archetypes.name: Spacecraft and Artificers
archetypes.plan: Use creatures that have already supplied an enters effect to station ships, then win through the air.
priorities: Early creatures that can defend while ships come online
Useful enters abilities and replay effects
Spacecraft with relevant text before they become creatures

formatNotes.draft: Take early defence alongside ships. A hand of only Spacecraft cannot station itself, and tapping your team costs attacks or blocks.
formatNotes.sealed: Choose this plan when your pool has enough actual creatures to defend and station. Evaluate the ship’s initial effect separately from its eventual body.

archetypes.name: Dilemma Control
archetypes.plan: Keep the board manageable while modal choices fuel your dilemma payoffs.
priorities: Interaction that works against the threats you expect
Modal spells and abilities that are useful without a payoff
A durable way to finish the game

formatNotes.draft: Count useful modal effects before relying on Seven of Nine. A mode is chosen before the spell resolves; repeated choices can provide a longer-game engine.
formatNotes.sealed: First establish early blockers and enough answers. Do not fill a control deck with weak modal spells just to trigger one uncommon.

archetypes.name: Klingons and Dies
archetypes.plan: Attack with replaceable bodies, then turn deaths and spare artifacts into more resources.
priorities: Cheap creatures and expendable tokens
Death payoffs and sacrifice outlets
Enough pressure that tokens can trade or connect

formatNotes.draft: Balance things to sacrifice with rewards for sacrificing them. Temporary Klingon tokens are useful fuel before their end-step sacrifice.
formatNotes.sealed: Look for overlapping creatures, interaction and death rewards. A sacrifice outlet with no spare bodies should not displace a card that stabilises the board.

archetypes.name: Away Team Landfall
archetypes.plan: Develop creatures, then turn repeated land entries into pressure and a wide board.
priorities: Playable early creatures
Landfall rewards and ways to put extra lands onto the battlefield
A plan for turning a wide board into damage

formatNotes.draft: Select land enablers with payoffs in mind, and keep enough creatures. An extra land entry matters more after a landfall permanent is in play.
formatNotes.sealed: Use landfall as an advantage inside a functional creature deck. Do not keep a fragile opening hand merely because it contains a payoff and several expensive spells.

archetypes.name: Doctors and Counters
archetypes.plan: Grow a board of creatures and use counters to turn attacks into sustained advantage.
priorities: Creatures worth improving
Counter sources that also develop the board
Ways for enhanced creatures to connect

formatNotes.draft: Build a curve before loading up on enhancement effects. Phlox recognises any counter on a creature, including charge counters on an active Spacecraft.
formatNotes.sealed: Check that your pool can deploy bodies on time. A counter engine is strongest when it improves creatures you were already happy to play.

archetypes.name: Borg Artifact Creatures
archetypes.plan: Build a board of artifact creatures, then turn shared bonuses and spare artifacts into a winning attack.
priorities: Artifact creatures across the mana curve
Multiple bodies from one card
Removal and payoffs that reward the artifacts you already want

formatNotes.draft: Count artifact creatures rather than all artifacts for Locutus. Clues and Food can support sacrifice costs but do not receive a creature bonus.
formatNotes.sealed: Start with the quality and number of artifact bodies you actually opened. Generic artifacts are not substitutes for creatures that can block and attack.

archetypes.name: Scientists and Noncreatures
archetypes.plan: Develop a creature board, then use noncreature spells to generate tempo and additional value.
priorities: Cheap noncreature spells with useful effects
Creatures that reward casting them
Threats that leave mana available for interaction

formatNotes.draft: Gray and Adira need a noncreature spell before combat and a creature worth copying. Spacecraft count as noncreature spells when cast.
formatNotes.sealed: Avoid a pool with too few actual creatures. Pick spell payoffs when your removal and other noncreature spells already support them.

archetypes.name: Archaeology Graveyard
archetypes.plan: Improve draws and stock the graveyard, then recover cards for repeated value.
priorities: Creatures that trade or supply an enters effect
Useful recursion and graveyard setup
A way to survive while the engine develops

formatNotes.draft: Vash rewards cards leaving your graveyard once each turn. Beam me up can supply that event without needing a reanimation spell.
formatNotes.sealed: Prefer effects with a useful floor over a fragile chain of graveyard pieces. Keep enough early creatures and removal to reach the long game.

archetypes.name: Command: 8+ Total Power
archetypes.plan: Build enough total creature power to unlock attack rewards and push through damage.
priorities: Efficient creatures across the early curve
Multiple bodies and ways to increase power
Removal or evasion to keep profitable attacks available

formatNotes.draft: The eight-power check counts creatures you control, including ones that are not attacking. Plan the threshold before declaring attackers.
formatNotes.sealed: Ask whether your creatures can attack into the board, not just reach eight power in an empty game. Keep interaction for a stalled battlefield.

archetypes.name: Strange New Worlds
archetypes.plan: Support a stable mana base while differently named lands improve your creatures and spells.
priorities: Early creatures and reliable coloured sources
Useful lands with distinct names
Payoffs that reward those names without demanding a bad mana base

formatNotes.draft: Count names on the battlefield, not land types or copies. Use dual lands and other useful nonbasics before adding a land solely to raise the count.
formatNotes.sealed: Build a mana base that casts your spells first. An off-colour land may add a name, but entering tapped or failing to supply your colours is a real cost.
